en: control of a company; right of management

examples.en: The president handed over management of the company to his son.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 경영권을 놓고 다투고 있어요.
examples.en: The two companies are fighting over control of management.

examples.ko: 대주주는 경영권 방어를 위해 주식을 더 샀어요.
examples.en: The major shareholder bought more shares to defend management control.

examples.ko: 아버지는 경영권 문제로 형제들과 사이가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: My father fell out with his brothers over the issue of who controls the business.

examples.ko: 새 투자자가 회사 경영권을 인수하겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The new investor said it would take over control of the company.

examples.ko: 경영권이 바뀐 뒤 회사 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After control of the company changed hands, the atmosphere changed.

explain: '경영권을 쥐다/넘기다/지키다'처럼 써요. 회사를 운영하는 힘을 말하고, 재산의 주인이 되는 '소유권'과는 달라요. 뉴스에서 주식이나 가족 회사 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs like '경영권을 쥐다', '넘기다' and '지키다'. It is the power to run a company, which is different from '소유권' (ownership). It appears often in news about stocks and family businesses.

examples.en: I got demerit points for not turning in homework.
If the demerits exceed ten points, they contact the parents.
I ran a signal and got 15 penalty points.
At this school, being late adds up demerits.

examples.ko: 벌점을 받으면 상점으로 줄일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you get demerits, you can also reduce them with merit points.
My driver's license was suspended because of penalty points.

explain: 벌점은 학교나 운전면허, 스포츠에서 규칙을 어길 때 쌓이는 점수예요. 반대로 잘했을 때 받는 점수는 '상점'이라고 해요. '벌점을 받다', '벌점이 쌓이다', '벌점을 매기다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: 벌점 are points that pile up when you break rules in school, driving or sports. The opposite, points for good behavior, are '상점'. It goes with '벌점을 받다', '벌점이 쌓이다' and '벌점을 매기다'.

examples.ko: 일정을 재조정해야 하면 하루 전까지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If the schedule needs to be adjusted, please tell us a day ahead.

examples.ko: 환율이 크게 올라서 수출 가격을 재조정하고 있어요.
examples.en: The exchange rate rose sharply, so we are readjusting export prices.
The meeting times overlapped, so I rearranged the appointment.

examples.ko: 예산을 재조정하면 새 프로젝트를 시작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we rearrange the budget, we can start the new project.
The school decided to revise its vacation plans.
The person in charge adjusted my working hours for me.

explain: 이미 정한 일정, 가격, 예산 같은 것을 상황에 맞게 다시 맞출 때 써요. 약속 시간만 바꾸는 가벼운 일에는 '바꾸다'나 '미루다'가 더 자연스러워요. 회사나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: Use it when you adjust something already decided, such as a schedule, price or budget, to fit the situation. For simply changing an appointment time, '바꾸다' or '미루다' sounds more natural. It shows up often at work and in the news.

examples.en: You need to tune the guitar strings for the sound to be right.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 회의 일정을 조율하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two companies are coordinating the meeting schedule.
The team leader smoothed out the differences of opinion among the staff.
Let's adjust our schedules and meet next week.
Could we adjust the price a little?

examples.ko: 서로 입장을 조율하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to reconcile each other's positions.

explain: 악기 소리를 맞추는 것에서 나와서, 사람들 사이의 일정이나 의견을 서로 맞추는 데도 써요. 직장에서 '일정을 조율하다'는 아주 자주 들려요. '조정하다'는 수치나 시간을 바꾸는 쪽이고, 조율하다는 여러 쪽이 서로 맞춰 가는 과정이 느껴져요.
explain_en: The word comes from tuning instruments and is also used for matching schedules or opinions between people. '일정을 조율하다' is very common at work. '조정하다' is more about changing a number or time, while 조율하다 conveys several sides adjusting to each other.

examples.en: The teacher gets every student involved in class.
We got the kids to take part in cleaning.
I want to involve the employees in the meeting.
If you involve guests in the event, they enjoy it more.
An event that involved the residents was held.
Don't force your younger sibling to join.

explain: 내가 참여하는 게 아니라 다른 사람이 참여하게 만들 때 써요. '참여하다'는 내가 하는 것, '참여시키다'는 상대를 끌어들이는 것이에요. 목적어에는 '을/를', 행사나 활동에는 '에'를 써요.
explain_en: Use this when you make someone else take part, not when you take part yourself. '참여하다' is what you do on your own; 참여시키다 brings someone else in. The person takes 을/를, and the event or activity takes 에.

examples.en: The company filled its staff shortage.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 직원 다섯 명을 충원할 예정이에요.
examples.en: We plan to add five employees within this year.
The team can only run if it adds players.
It took time to fill the vacancy.

examples.ko: 아직 충원하지 못해서 모두 야근을 해요.
examples.en: We haven't been able to add staff yet, so everyone works overtime.

examples.ko: 새로 충원한 사람들이 잘 적응하고 있어요.
examples.en: The newly added people are adjusting well.

explain: '보충하다'는 물건이나 내용에도 쓰지만 '충원하다'는 사람, 즉 인원이나 인력을 채울 때만 써요. '인력을 충원하다', '결원을 충원하다'처럼 목적어가 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: '보충하다' can be used for things or content too, but '충원하다' is only for filling people, meaning headcount or manpower. Its objects are fixed, as in '인력을 충원하다' and '결원을 충원하다'.
